questions.q: As of December 31, 2025, what happened to Workflow Rules and Process Builder?
options: They were immediately deleted from every org
They were merged into a single new automation tool
Salesforce ended support (no more bug fixes or new features), but existing active automation keeps running
They became available only in sandbox orgs
questions.explain: End of support means no further bug fixes or features from Salesforce — it is not a shutdown. Existing workflow rules and processes continue to execute.

questions.q: What does the Migrate to Flow tool convert, and in what ratio?
options: All workflow rules on an object at once, into a single combined flow
One workflow rule or process at a time, into exactly one new flow (1-to-1)
Apex triggers into Flow elements
Flows back into Workflow Rules for legacy compatibility
questions.explain: Migrate to Flow performs a strict one-to-one conversion: one existing workflow rule or process becomes one new flow.

questions.q: Why does a workflow rule with only field updates get converted into a before-save flow specifically?
options: Before-save flows are required by Salesforce for all migrations
Before-save flows update the record in memory before the save, making them significantly faster than after-save flows
Before-save flows support email actions better than after-save flows
It's a random default with no performance reasoning
questions.explain: A before-save flow is meaningfully faster for simple field updates, so the tool uses it whenever the rule only updates fields (no email/outbound message/time-dependent actions).

questions.q: What is the state of the original workflow rule and the new flow immediately after running Migrate to Flow?
options: The workflow rule is deleted and the new flow is immediately active
Both are active simultaneously by default
The workflow rule stays active and the new flow is created inactive, until you switch activations
Both are inactive until manually reviewed by Salesforce Support
questions.explain: The migration doesn't change live automation immediately — the old rule keeps running while the new flow sits inactive for testing, until a one-click switch activates it and deactivates the old rule.

questions.q: If an object has eight workflow rules and all eight are migrated individually with Migrate to Flow, what problem remains?
options: None — the migration is fully complete and well-architected
The flows will automatically merge themselves after 30 days
Salesforce will reject more than one migrated flow per object
The resulting eight separate flows recreate the automation-sprawl problem; they still need consolidating into one flow per object per trigger context
questions.explain: Migrate to Flow converts syntax 1-to-1 but doesn't address architecture — eight separate migrated flows still need to be consolidated per the one-flow-per-object-per-context pattern.
